analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/developer/build.md (only the head excerpt was supplied; no changed lines are identifiable from it) and docs/developer/test.md (date bump, hunk at ~884, new paragraph at ~4497). There are no code, auth, crypto or billing changes. Security-relevant content is in test.md. The coordinator build-qualification test paths were removed and replaced by a pointer to the external darkbloom-platform repo. Both the replaced paragraph and the new paragraph near line 4497 now call hardware smoke optional and not a per-release gate. That wording diverges from the canonical statements that signed-artifact and physical-Mac qualification are required and are never inferred from CI, and from build.md lines 1095 and 1117. Relevant threats: T-054, T-052, T-056, TB-011, A-017. The mitigation test references in T-054 may now point at tests that live outside this repo. The next pass should check whether other docs or threat-model entries cite the removed coordinator test paths, and whether the platform repo still has the publish/revoke race and admin-key rejection tests. The base text of test.md (lines 1-438) was supplied only for the head of the file, so the base side of the hunks near lines 884 and 4497 could not be checked beyond the patch.

findings.detail: This hunk replaces the paragraph naming the coordinator build-qualification regressions: the store, authorization and release-route tests for publish/revoke races, cache fencing, lease expiry, and rejection of admin-owned inference keys. It now says the tests are retained only as an earlier snapshot and live in another repository. It also states that hardware smoke is optional and not a per-release gate. The canonical threat model (header notes, T-054, TB-011) still says final signed-artifact and physical-Mac qualification is an operator evidence requirement before serving is enabled, and is never inferred from a CI green check. build.md (lines 1095 and 1117) still requires signed-Mac qualification. The result is contradictory guidance: an operator or release engineer could promote an unqualified signed build and rely on CI alone. Fix: reconcile the wording so optional smoke is clearly distinct from the required durable build qualification and revocation evidence. Update T-054 and the canonical mitigation references to point at the platform tests that now own those controls.
findings.title: Test guide drops release-gate language that T-054 and the canonical context still require
